props.title: Blue and Clear
props.caption: one shader on one plane mesh: the finished water, built in this film

B01.capture_spec: C01: scene water_scene.gd, shader 06-shore-foam, plane cut 127 x 127, iso camera, wave clock driven by the capture clock (W_FOLLOW), Forward+, the whole beat plus 1.0 s tail.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'Blue and Clear' (serif 40) top-left; the finished water fills the framed window: blue and see-through over sand, a foam net, glints, rolling waves, a white shore line on the beach, the teal buoy and the cream crate riding the waves.
B01.motion_claim: The waves roll and the buoy and crate rise and fall with them while the foam net drifts: the whole film's result before any code.

show.event: buoy and crate ride a crest

B01.why: A real render is the honest first picture of what a shader can make; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: Left to right on the cream stage: a flat isometric plane tile labelled 'PlaneMesh'; an outlined slot labelled 'Material Override' holding a round preview tile labelled 'ShaderMaterial'; a small code-card icon labelled 'shader'. An outline box labelled 'MeshInstance3D' encloses the plane and the slot. Arrow shapes link them in turn: mesh to node, material into the slot, shader into the material.
B02.motion_claim: Three links draw in the order the voice names them, ending with the node holding the material.
B02.runner_up: ShaderLab: a real Inspector frame from the editor driver
B02.why: The three-link chain is a structure with a direction; a drawing shows which holds which. A real Inspector frame comes in the last act.

cues.label: fragment: runs once for each pixel the shape covers
albedo: the base color of a 3D surface

props.caption: built-in: a value the engine hands to a function

B03.capture_spec: C02: scene water_scene.gd, W_LATE: the water plane has no material until 55 % of the beat, then 01-blue.gdshader is assigned; iso camera, Forward+.
B03.visual_intent: Code card with all eleven lines of 01-blue.gdshader at left (three cue labels land on lines 1, 8 and 9); at right the real render: a pale unshaded-looking grey plane over the sand until 55 % of the beat, then the plane turns solid blue with the sun's glare.
B03.motion_claim: A plain grey plane turns blue the moment the shader is assigned, while the three code lines light up.
B03.why: The first shader is eleven lines: code and its real result side by side show that those lines are the blue.

cues.label: uniform: set from outside; every pixel sees the same one
source_color: the numbers are sRGB; convert to light first

props.caption: typed 0.10, 0.45, 0.70 reads 25, 115, 178 in an unshaded test, Forward+

B04.capture_spec: C03: scene water_scene.gd, shader 01-blue, water_color set to green-teal at 35 %, violet at 62 %, back to the default 0.10, 0.45, 0.70 at 82 %. The 25, 115, 178 reading is the unshaded test E1 (evidence/planning-checks/RESULTS.md).
B04.visual_intent: Code card with the uniform lines; the real cove whose water turns green-teal, then violet, then back to blue; the pill '25 115 178' lands when the default colour returns, with the caption naming the unshaded test.
B04.motion_claim: The uniform is a dial: the colour changes three times without touching the code.
B04.runner_up: manim: a typed colour and a pixel byte triple
B04.why: The dial is something to watch turn; the measured bytes arrive as one caption-backed pill, on the real shader.

cues.label: roughness: 0 is a mirror, 1 is fully matte

props.caption: roughness 0.9 down to 0.03

B05.capture_spec: C04: scene water_scene.gd, shader 01-blue, roughness swept linearly from 0.9 to 0.03 across the beat.
B05.visual_intent: Code card (the four fragment lines, ROUGHNESS lit); the real cove with the sun's reflection: a wide soft smear at the start that shrinks to a tight bright oval as the ramp marker runs from 0.9 to 0.03.
B05.motion_claim: The reflection tightens and sharpens as roughness falls.
B05.why: The sun's reflection on the real plane is the evidence; a lobe drawing would be a model of it.

props.caption: stage 01, solid, swapped for stage 02: one more line

B06.capture_spec: C05: scene water_scene.gd, solid 01-blue on the water, swapped (swap_shader) at 40 % of the beat for 02-transparent on the same material, opacity set to 1.0 then easing to 0.7.
B06.visual_intent: Code card with the stage-two fragment (ALPHA line lit); the real cove: a solid blue plane hiding the floor, then at 40 % the surface turns see-through and the sand, the rock and the buoy's underside appear under it.
B06.motion_claim: One line is added and the sand and the rocks appear through the water.
B06.why: The floor appearing under the real water is the proof that one line did it.

props.caption: opacity: how much of the surface shows

B07.capture_spec: C06: scene water_scene.gd, shader 02-transparent, opacity 1.0 held to 20 %, down to 0.3 by 42 % (held to 56 %), up to 0.7 by 72 %.
B07.visual_intent: Code card (fragment, ALPHA lit); the real cove going from hiding everything (1.0) through almost invisible (0.3) to the readable default (0.7); the pill shows the opacity at each hold.
B07.motion_claim: The water fades from solid to almost gone and settles at point seven.
B07.why: Three holds on the real water let the viewer pick the value by eye, which is how the default was chosen.

B08.visual_intent: Left: three flat swatches in the measured colours: water (25, 115, 178), sand (184, 157, 110) and a result swatch (108, 129, 162), joined by the sum '70 percent water plus 30 percent sand' drawn as two proportion bars. Under them two number rows: 'predicted 108, 129, 161' and 'screen 108, 129, 162'. Right: the real Forward+ test render (captures/blend-fp.png through lab_window) with one grey-backed terracotta ring on the probe point (plate over sand). Every number is a measured or computed figure from FACTCHECK.
B08.motion_claim: The bars slide together into the result swatch and the two number rows land one under the other, differing by one in the last place.

show.event: screen row and ring on the render

B08.runner_up: ShaderLab with the test render and readouts
B08.why: A sum with real numbers is a Manim kind of picture; the real render is inset so the figures are never free-floating.

B09.visual_intent: Two real test renders side by side (captures/blend-fp.png labelled 'Forward+', captures/blend-compat.png labelled 'Compatibility'), the probe point ringed in each; under them the red channel read: 108 and 71. A number line 0 to 255 under both shows two ticks, 'typed-number mix' at 73 and 'linear-light blend' at 108: the Compatibility reading sits on 73 and the Forward+ reading on 108.
B09.motion_claim: The two readings drop onto the number line one after the other and snap to the tick they match.

show.event: Forward+ reading 108 lands on the linear tick
Compatibility reading 71 lands on the typed tick

B09.why: Two renderers, one pixel, one number line: the choice of arithmetic is the claim, and a number line shows which arithmetic each renderer used.

props.title: render_mode: the three defaults
rows: Mix blend mode (alpha is transparency), default.
Only draw depth for opaque geometry (not transparent).
props.note: Godot 4.7 docs · spatial shaders · render modes · read 2026-10-16

B10.visual_intent: Three rows, one per render mode in the shader's second line, each with the docs' own words in a second column; the row for the mode being spoken is highlighted.
B10.motion_claim: The highlight steps down the table as the voice names each mode.
B10.why: The docs' exact words belong in a table the viewer can read; a page screenshot would be too small to read at four K.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · water made to write depth at 78 %
props.caption: a red plane under the water: drawn on top, then hidden
props.code:
render_mode blend_mix, depth_draw_opaque, cull_back;
render_mode blend_mix, depth_draw_always, cull_back;

cues.label: depth_draw_opaque: the water writes no depth

B11.capture_spec: C37: scene water_scene.gd, W_EXTRA=sort adds a red see-through plane (alpha 0.6) at y = -0.4 UNDER the water with its node origin nearer the camera; shader 02-transparent swapped at 78 % of the beat for 02a-depth-draw-always on the same material; iso camera, Forward+. Measured in evidence/planning-checks (E16): no render_mode line and the written defaults render pixel-identical; depth_draw_always hides the plane (56,099 pixels differ by more than 8 levels).
B11.visual_intent: Code card with the two render_mode lines (the default first, depth_draw_always second); the real cove with a red see-through plane lying under the water yet painted over it at the bottom of the frame; at 78 % of the beat the plane vanishes and the water shows blue and clean there.
B11.motion_claim: A red plane that should be under the water is painted on top of it, then disappears when the water is made to write depth.

show.event: depth_draw_opaque line, red plane over the water

B11.runner_up: manim: the draw order drawn (kept in _superseded/)
B11.why: A real plane drawn in the wrong order is the claim itself; the drawing could only say it.

props.title: What transparent materials cannot do
props.note: Godot 4.7 docs · spatial shaders · E8: 0.500 m.

B12.visual_intent: Three rows: casts shadows, appears in the depth texture, appears in the screen texture; each answered 'cannot' by the docs; the depth row also carries the measured gap of 0.500 m.
B12.motion_claim: The rows light in the order the voice lists them, the depth row last and longest.

show.event: depth row with the measured gap

B12.runner_up: Manim: a shadow and a depth strip
B12.why: Three yes-or-no facts with one measured number are a table's job; a drawing would add nothing the words do not carry.
